targets.authors: Cichocka, A., Bilewicz, M., Jost, J. T., Marrouch, N., & Witkowska, M.
targets.title: On the grammar of politics—or why conservatives prefer nouns.
targets.evidence_quote: We decided to conduct a conceptual replication of Cichocka et al.’s (2016) Study 1.
targets.outcome_quote:
Cichocka et al. (2016) Study 1 found that social, but not economic, conservatism is
associated with noun preference, and that PNS accounted for this relationship. We were able to
replicate the effects of social and not economic conservatism on both PNS and noun preference,
but not the relationship between PNS and noun preference.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors report replication of the conservatism relationship alongside failure of the PNS relationship; their verdict is explicitly partial. Other cited works motivate the measures and theory and are not separately re-tested.

reasoning: Full preprint title and Jarret T. Crawford match the assignment. A new American MTurk sample conceptually re-tests Cichocka et al. Study 1. Reference does not print a DOI.
